column2: Piedmont has secured Lombardy and the southern question can no longer remain a contest between provisional administrations and Bourbon ministers. Delegates assemble in Turin to settle the plebiscites and place the peninsula beneath the Savoyard crown. The temporal government in Rome will remain separate under a foreign guarantee.
Prepare the settlement of the Italian kingdom.
The Plebiscites Are Ratified in Turin

The southern and central provinces accept union under Victor Emmanuel. The remaining administrations hand their affairs to Turin, and the civil conflict gives way to the proclamation of a national kingdom. Rome and Viterbo remain with the Holy See. The Venetian and Alpine questions await later settlements.
Accept the plebiscites and proclaim the kingdom.
A French Guarantee for the Holy See

The Italian kingdom has absorbed the southern and central provinces, while the Pope retains Rome and Viterbo. France offers protection for the remaining temporal state. The guarantee preserves its separate government and leaves the Roman question unresolved between Paris, Turin and the Holy See.
Place the remaining Papal State under French protection.
